aliases.alias: Land Adjacent To Crosshill Road, Bishopbriggs

summary: Apatura proposes a 300MW AI data centre campus with a co-located 500MW battery energy storage system on land adjacent to Crosshill Road, Westerhill, north-east of Bishopbriggs, within East Dunbartonshire Council's adopted Westerhill Regeneration Area masterplan. The data centre would be consented by the council; the BESS is intended to be consented separately under section 36 via the Energy Consents Unit. As of July 2026 the project is at pre-application stage: an EIA screening opinion (TP/ED/25/0245) concluded EIA is required, and a Proposal of Application Notice (TP/ED/25/0428) was lodged in August 2025, but no full planning application or s36 application has been located.
maturity_explanation: Early development: EIA screening decided (EIA required, 8 Jul 2025), PAN lodged (1 Aug 2025, closed 16 Sep 2025) and public consultation held Sep 2025; developer states a NESO grid offer was accepted June 2025. No validated full planning application or ECU s36 application found as of 30 Jul 2026 (APRS recorded status still pre-planning on 23 Feb 2026).
anticipated_construction_start: 2027 (developer indicative timeline; earlier panel version said 2026)

latest_development.headline: APRS re-checked the case and recorded it still at pre-planning; press reporting (Feb 2026) said an application to East Dunbartonshire Council was expected imminently

unknowns: Site area in hectares (not stated in any located source; red-line boundary shown only as consultation graphics)
Whether the full planning application has been submitted (developer timeline said Q4 2025-Q2 2026; none located on the portal as of 30 Jul 2026)
Whether an s36 application for the 500MW BESS has been lodged with the Energy Consents Unit (ECU register returned an application error; only the ECU screening consultation EDC00006158 is evidenced)
East Dunbartonshire Council's formal position on the proposal (no committee report or council statement located)
Split between IT load and total demand within the 300MW figure ('demand utility capacity' per PAN; building-level labels sum to 240MW)
Landownership of the site and any option agreement
Water demand figures (developer states closed-loop cooling but gives no volumes)
Economic analysis methodology and author (panels credit an unnamed independent consultant)
